instructs: Boot triad first: know what model you are, what session root actually loaded (.claude/ binds only when fleet-manager IS the root — a satellite root or the bare /home/user parent silently loads nothing), and what you can do; default posture is 'you have full capability — act'.

Cold orientation is README.md's six mandatory reads (CLAUDE.md, docs/intent.md, docs/current-state.md, the consolidation program PAIRED with the 2026-08-08 agent-operating-environment roadmap, docs/fleet-account-2026-07-26.md, docs/owner-reflection-2026-07-21.md), then state purpose, era, what the owner is working on, and the next step.

Walk the deeper read path in order (owner reflection → current-state → roadmap → program → foundation-continuation findings + certainty legend MEASURED/OWNER/REASONED/UNVERIFIED → fleet account → owner-queue → PROJECT-CLOSEOUT §3), then the Layer-2 docs/repos/<name>/README.md for the repo you are on, then docs/owner-comments/<name>/README.md before acting.

Never write down a limitation: a refused call is transient classifier state, route around it, leave no wall behind. When the owner states something about this estate, act on it rather than probing to check him.

Never delete a trigger (it raises an approval prompt in automode and stalls the session until he is physically back); disable with update_trigger enabled:false instead. Do not send_later to poll a PR — use subscribe_pr_activity, and poll check-runs to a terminal state inside the turn.
Vertex-first for Gemini: GEMINI_API_KEY is free tier, the paid project bills his card on generativelanguage; default to Vertex for volume/image/video and say out loud in the card when you fell back.
Wait for @codex (~5.5 min); read /pulls/{n}/comments (findings are inline, not in the review body); never merge a PR whose requested review has not answered on the current head.
Do not write about a file you have not opened; if you cannot open it, say the line is inferred.
Verify before fold, with real exit codes — never $? after a pipe. One local gate: python3 bootstrap.py check --strict (the check list lives in scripts/preflight.py, not in prose).

Session discipline: born-red session card at birth, session close flips it complete last, land on green, update the program's §7 ledger + NOW pointer and docs/owner-queue.md, drive any PR you opened to a terminal state.

Invoking the routed skill IS part of the task (image-prompt, prompt-preflight, intake, capability-probe, delegate-read, owner-brief, session-close, release, etc.); for estate-wide 'what did other sessions do', run tools/estate_activity.py refresh and read docs/activity/ — this repo's .sessions/ is fleet-manager's work alone.
Answer the Stop hook's block inside the reply the owner reads, using the [survived]/[conceded]/[partial] disposition vocabulary.
The seven-entry trap register (docs/traps.md) is binding: an entry without a delivering route is unfinished work; a trap earns a place only after two instances or one with real cost.

Working style: one thing at a time finished properly, small PRs, records may grow but instructions may not (the fix for an unfollowed rule is a mechanism, never another statement of it), ask immediately and keep working, stop almost never.
Precedence: the live owner outranks any stored order; the committed tree beats any doc's claim; live surfaces beat dated records.

prose_only_rules: The six-read cold-orientation mandate. Nothing checks that a session read anything before acting — check_boot_path/check_orientation_budget grade the DOC surface (does the path exist, does it fit the budget), never the session's behaviour. A boot that skips all six looks identical to one that did them.

The boot-triad root diagnosis. CLAUDE.md documents that a satellite root or the bare /home/user parent silently loads no hooks, no skills, no read path — and the only remedy offered is 'run tools/install_root_hooks.py --apply by hand'. In exactly the failure case, nothing is loaded to tell you so. This is a rule that cannot deliver itself.

'Invoking the skill IS part of the task' — the whole task→skill routing table. No hook injects a skill, no checker records whether one fired; the table itself says a skill you didn't load can't bind you (PL-013) and then relies on prose to load it.
'Read docs/owner-comments/<name>/README.md and open the Unconsumed records BEFORE acting.' The consume workflow is schema-checked and regression-tested; whether you READ before acting is not.

'Never merge a PR you asked Codex to review before it answers' / wait ~5.5 min / read the inline comments. TRAP-007 states plainly there is no checker — the verdict-at-head test is PR state, not tree state — and it recurred at least twice after being written down.
Vertex-first for Gemini. The route puts the doc in front of you; nothing checks which key or endpoint a call actually used, or whether a paid fallback was declared in the card as required.

'Run tools/estate_activity.py refresh before answering anything estate-wide.' Delivered by one UserPromptSubmit route; no gate notices a stale docs/activity/estate-log.md — it was 2 days stale on the estate's busiest day and only a hand refresh caught it.

'Do not pipe the command whose exit code you need' in PROSE and in chat replies. check_pipe_exit_code.py deliberately scans executable surfaces only (18 files), so the trap as committed to the owner in a message is uncovered by design.

R28's repo-qualify-every-owner/repo#N rule, declared 'live and estate-general' in CLAUDE.md — no route, no checker, and it lives inside docs/playbook.md, a file the same paragraph labels mixed-era history.

The working-style block in full: one thing at a time / small PRs / 'records may grow, instructions may not' / 'ask immediately, stop almost never' / cleanup with a stated reason. Entirely unmechanised — including the meta-rule that unmechanised rules are the wrong fix.
The [survived]/[conceded]/[partial] disposition vocabulary for adversarial review. The Stop hook forces the block; nothing checks the reply uses the vocabulary or that the tally is countable.

The certainty legend (MEASURED / MEASURED-PRIOR / OWNER / REASONED / REVIEWED / UNVERIFIED / NOT-VERIFIABLE) that 'governs how to read every dated claim in this repo'. One Edit/Write route fires on the MEASURED tag; the other six tags are unrouted and unchecked.

biggest_gap: Everything that happens BEFORE the first tool call, and everything that happens in a chat reply, is unenforced. Every mechanism here binds to a tool_input (PreToolUse routes and guards) or to a committed file (bootstrap check, substrate-gate CI). So the two highest-stakes instructions in the repo — the six-read cold orientation, and 'invoke the routed skill' — have no delivery at all, and the trap register concedes the same hole for replies (the session that shipped TRAP-004 committed TRAP-004 in the same message and the register caught nothing, correctly). Compounding it: the entire apparatus is conditional on fleet-manager being the session root, and in the two cases where it is not, the failure mode is documented as silent and no-error — the hooks that would warn you are the ones that did not load. Second-order, a dozen written checkers sit unwired since the roster workflows were retired, which means the repo's checker inventory reads far stronger than its actually-running set (preflight's 5 legs + repo_checks.sh's 2-5).
portable_lesson: Two, and they are the same idea at different layers. (1) The trap lifecycle: mistake → trap entry → route/hook reminder → deterministic checker where possible, with the register declaring that an entry WITHOUT a delivering route is unfinished work, and a public coverage table naming which traps are still route-only or undelivered. That converts 'we wrote it down' from an accomplishment into a visible debt — and the honest 'TRAP-005 is undelivered and here is why' row is what makes the rest credible. (2) The doc-route coverage validator: a route table decays by pointing at a doc that no longer covers its trigger, so check_doc_routes.py requires that at least one of a route's `when` patterns actually OCCURS in one of its docs, and fails otherwise. Every kit adopter shipping a doc-injection hook needs that check, because a hook that confidently misroutes is worse than no hook — the session stops looking. Bonus, cheap and general: the host-owned scripts/repo_checks.sh extension point planted in the kit-owned workflow, which ended the class where every upgrade silently dropped hand-added gate steps.

instructs: Boot triad every session (Q-0270): state what model you are, where you are running, and what that venue can do — the model family goes in the card's `📊 Model:` line, family-level only.

Read in a fixed order at session start: `.claude/CLAUDE.md` → `docs/collaboration-model.md` → `docs/current-state.md` → `.session-journal.md` → `docs/AGENT_ORIENTATION.md` for the task-specific route.
Precedence is explicit and repeated: source code and merged PRs > `.claude/CLAUDE.md` > `docs/current-state.md` > the journal. When a doc and a source file disagree, the source file wins.

Do NOT self-edit `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, hooks, or `.claude/settings.json` on your own initiative (Q-0106). Propose rule changes as a router Q-block in the DISCUSS lane of `docs/owner/maintainer-question-router.md`. The one exception is a change the maintainer directs in-session, which ships with its provenance Q-number. In a fully autonomous session CLAUDE.md is read-only to the agent.

Understand-and-reflect (Q-0254): before substantive work, state back inline the FULLER picture built from a fragmentary ask, including the specs it implied but did not say. When feasibility is uncertain, surface the possibility space first. Target the most advanced capability reachable by the simplest implementation.

Decide-and-flag over route-up (Q-0240/Q-0241): anything reversible until a downstream gate is decided by the agent with a one-line rationale and a flag on the run report, not parked for the owner. Only genuine product/intent ambiguity routes to the router. The sole stop-and-wait is *executing* something irreversible before the gate.
Session prompts are guidance, not orders (Q-0120) — and the same holds for any cross-agent output (a Codex/Gemini/ChatGPT review): verify each specific against shipped source before acting.

Claim before starting (Q-0126/Q-0195): scan `docs/owner/claims/` and open PRs for lane overlap, create one file `docs/owner/claims/<branch>.md`, delete it at session close. One file per claim, never a shared list — a real-merge simulation measured the shared-append ledger at ~98% conflict vs 0% per-file.
Open a PR every session, READY not draft, within the first ~2 minutes and BEFORE the build work (Q-0052/Q-0103/Q-0189) — the in-flight signal is the whole point.

Born-red session card (Q-0133): create `.sessions/<date>-<slug>.md` with `> **Status:** `in-progress`` in the FIRST commit; flip to `complete` as the deliberate LAST step so the merge gate goes green.
A session is not done until its PR reaches a terminal state — merged or closed (Q-0103). Never leave a session PR open at session end.

Merging is normal agent work (Q-0123/Q-0191): merge your own green PR directly, or let `auto-merge-enabler` land it. Never route a mergeable green PR to the owner. Only gate is CI green plus the `do-not-automerge` carve-out. `needs-hermes-review` is retired.
Merging IS deploying (Q-0193): Railway auto-redeploys `worker` on merge to main. Never tell the maintainer to restart or deploy a merge.
Never generalize a specific permission refusal into a standing wall — attempt-once, report the refusal verbatim, do not write it into the docs.

Match CI exactly: always `python3.10 -m <tool>`, never bare `black`/`pytest`/`python3 -m`. Run `python3.10 scripts/check_quality.py --full` before pushing. Tool versions pinned identically in `code-quality.yml`, `requirements-dev.txt` and `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.

A green check that contradicts visible evidence is a bug in the check, not a clearance (Q-0120) — the canonical #763 false-green, where both checkers matched `Merge pull request #N` but not the MCP `Merge PR #N:` style.

Five non-negotiable CodeGraph rules: `dead-unresolved` is ~100% false-positive here; same-name functions merge caller graphs; Discord decorators create invisible entry points; empty `callees` means read the source; EventBus/registry/dynamic edges are invisible to both CodeGraph and Grimp.

Architecture layer table with one zero-tolerance rule: any new `services/ → views/` import is an immediate ERROR. Adding to `architecture_rules/` YAML is the only valid bypass — never suppress the check.

DB/mutation discipline: never `pool.execute()`/`conn.execute()` outside `utils/db/`; always write through the domain's `*_mutation.py`; always emit `audit_events.emit_audit_action()`; always use `settings_keys` constants.

Four mandatory session enders: groom one idea (Q-0015), contribute one genuinely-believed new idea (Q-0089), review the previous session plus one system improvement (Q-0102), and run a documentation audit (Q-0104). Forced filler is explicitly worse than none.

Friction → guard (Q-0194): convert any workflow interruption into the cheapest ENFORCING prevention before the session ends, in order checker/CI/test → hook → journal Rule. 'Enforce, don't exhort' (Q-0132). Ownership split: docs/test/checker guards ship free; hook / settings.json / CLAUDE.md rules are owner-gated.
Fix docs/ledger drift on sight (Q-0166) — the 30-PR reconciliation is a failsafe, not a licence to defer drift you already spotted. Benign newest-merge lag is the only exception.

Reconciliation + planning pass at every 30th PR (Q-0107), docs-only, no `disbot/` code — but a MANUALLY started session does not run it unless the owner asks (Q-0124); the `Recon: DUE` banner is a signal for the routine only.

Idea order ≠ implementation order (Q-0172): capture into `docs/ideas/` first, don't derail the current task — but any agent may promote idea → plan → implementation with no approval, provided it is flagged on the `⚑ Self-initiated:` run-report line.

Every session log carries a required run-report footer (⚑ Owner decisions / ⚑ Owner manual steps / ⚑ Self-initiated / Run type / ↪ Next, `none` when empty), a telemetry table, a `Context delta` section produced by a seven-question reflection interview, and a `📊 Model:` line.

Concurrent-chat safety: `.claude/CLAUDE.md` is split into `<!-- SECTION_START/END -->` ownership blocks and each parallel chat edits ONE block; the question router is append-only; `.sessions/` is per-file.
Owner shorthand (review · status · routines · plan · ship · groom) maps to workflows in `docs/owner/fleet-vocab.md`; the executable ones are `.claude/skills/`.

Fleet reading path (Q-0272): read-only access to all ~19 sibling repos is standing-authorized via raw.githubusercontent/git clone, no `add_repo` needed to read; writes stay scoped to this repo and cross-repo work routes via the fleet-manager inbox.
superbot is FROZEN as the behavioural oracle for the `superbot-next` rebuild: kit method and records work is in scope, the repo's BEHAVIOUR is not.
Adopted tooling carries a provenance + reliability header with date, an 'unverified — confirm against ground truth' note, and an explicit 'delete this if it proves unreliable' kill-switch (Q-0105).

portable_lesson: Two, and both are mechanism rather than prose. (1) **The born-red session card (Q-0133).** One per-session file, `.sessions/<date>-<slug>.md`, is *both* the start-declaration and the end-record. It is created in the session's FIRST commit with `> **Status:** \`in-progress\``, which opens the PR red — `check_session_gate` in `code-quality.yml` holds the merge — and the deliberate LAST action of the session is flipping the badge to `complete`. This makes close-out documentation structurally impossible to skip without also failing to ship, and it converts "always write your session log" from an exhortation into a merge gate. Crucially the gate engages **only when a PR adds a card**, so workflow-authored PRs are never deadlocked. Any repo with a session-log convention should be gating on the badge rather than reminding about the log. (2) **Glob-triggered `.claude/rules/*.md`.** Three small files (`mutation-and-db.md`, `discord-views.md`, `context-compiler.md`) carry YAML `globs:` frontmatter (`disbot/services/**/*.py`, `disbot/views/**/*.py`, `docs/agent/**`) and load automatically when a matching file is opened — the layer rules arrive at the moment of the edit, not at boot. Paired with a `/pre-edit-check` skill that front-loads the *command* half (`context_map.py <file>` + `check_architecture.py --mode strict`), this is the cleanest instance in the estate of the estate's own doctrine ("the fix for an unfollowed rule is a mechanism that delivers it at the right moment"). fleet-manager's `route_docs.py` does the same job for provider docs; the glob-frontmatter form is cheaper (no hook, no route registry) and should ship in the kit as the default pattern for path-scoped rules.

The CAPABILITIES discovery rule, stated as a four-step sequence: check the file → check the env → attempt once and capture the exact error → append the finding in the same session. Never write a standing limitation; a refused call is transient platform state, not a property of the tool.

Session-card discipline (`.sessions/README.md`): the card is the session's FIRST commit, born red (`Status: in-progress`), flipped to `complete` as the deliberate LAST step. Required markers: Status badge, Session idea, Previous-session review, and the model line `- **📊 Model:** <model> · <effort> · <task-class>`.

The model line is self-reported at FAMILY level from your own harness (`fable-5`, `opus-4.8`) — never an exact model-ID token, never copied from an external surface (schedule/Routines screens are evidenced to misattribute). Effort is a real tier (low/medium/high); `unrecorded` is terminal-only, for retroactive repair of someone else's card, never your own live one.
Routine-fired lab sessions additionally carry `Run type: routine · lab` in the card header; owner-started sessions omit it.

An auto-drafted card is a starting point, not a close-out: resolve every `[[fill:]]` slot and verify the evidence before flipping the badge. Drafted ≠ completed and the checker reports them distinctly.
Friction becomes a GUARD RECIPE, not a symptom note: name the function + file + test target for the next session. The stated cost of ignoring this is a re-derivation grep pass (the KL-0→KL-1 lesson).

Program law, cite-never-copy: `docs/program/rulings.md` is the single canonical home of `[PL-NNN]` rulings. Append-only, superseded never rewritten, provenance mandatory on every block. Consumers cite PL-IDs; a copied ruling body in an adopter repo is 'drift by construction'.

PL-001 decide-and-flag: default is decide, don't route — including calls that feel architectural or 'the owner's call'. Only a decision that would EXECUTE something irreversible before the gate is a stop-and-ask.
PL-002 never-wait: silence = consent = done; live-green is the agent's own gate; the reversibility rider means the destructive tier executes via the reversible-equivalent path rather than waiting.

PL-006 source wins: cross-agent output (Codex/Gemini/ChatGPT) is INPUT to verify against shipped source, never orders; and a green check that contradicts visible evidence is a bug in the check, not a clearance.

PL-007 enforce, don't exhort: any friction is converted to the cheapest enforcing prevention before the session ends, in a stated ladder — checker/CI/test → hook → written rule. A claim that must stay true is CI-backed or explicitly date-stamped as a snapshot.

PL-013 inhabiting beats observing: read access is not integration; a convention committed to docs does not govern a session that merely reads it; decomposition is an environment property, so size a request to the surface that will run it.

PL-014 a measured claim carries its instrument: numbers in measurement docs carry a LABELLED provenance statement (`measured` with method AND instrument resolution / `inferred` / `assumed`). Deliberately advisory at the gate.

PL-015 verification is an independent check that could have failed: 'if the check is I read it and it looked right, nothing was checked' — plus two corollaries, fix the rule set not the named symptom, and point the script at the artifact that will actually be graded.

Control-bus ritual (`control/README.md`): claim FIRST and build second (one executor per ORDER, one file per claim under `control/claims/`), write a heartbeat to `control/status.md` every session and every routine wake, delegated writes are MARKED and the member repo POINTS at its live tally.
`control/inbox.md` is pure-append with ORDER grammar; the manager flips new→done.
Search hygiene: `bootstrap.py` (~12k generated lines) and `.substrate/` are kit machinery, not project code — exclude them from repo-wide searches.

Architecture/import law: `src/engine/` is source of truth (stdlib-only, no print/assert/subprocess, atomic writes); `dist/bootstrap.py` is GENERATED and byte-pinned by CI; planted docs are output, never engine input; engine modules import stdlib and each other only.
Run `python3.10 -m pytest tests/ -q` before every push.

biggest_gap:
"The kit's flagship doctrine is the one thing it has no mechanism for. PL-007 ('durable behavior comes from mechanized enforcement, never from per-session discipline') and PL-013 ('readable is not binding — a convention committed to docs does not govern a session that merely reads it') are the program's core claims, and both are delivered as prose in `docs/program/rulings.md`, checked by a script that only validates heading grammar and provenance fields. The register is a beautifully enforced container for entirely unenforced content.

The structural cause is visible in the payload: **the kit ships the CHECKED tier and the SKILL tier, but not the ROUTED tier.** `.claude/skills/` is in the copy loop; `.claude/hooks/` explicitly is not (stated in `change_guard.py`'s own docstring). So every mechanism in this estate that delivers a rule at the moment of action — 71 doc-routes, read-before-write, change_guard, git_state_guard, the trigger deny, the Stop review — was hand-built in fleet-manager and reaches zero adopters. An adopter repo gets doctrine it can read and checkers that fire after the fact, which is precisely the observer position PL-013 says is not binding. The kit tells 12 repos that reading isn't enough, using a delivery mechanism that is reading.

Secondary and compounding: the kit-side and host-side copies of `check_no_false_walls.py` have already diverged (kit #587 fixed three false-negative families in the engine copy that the fm fork does not have), and the host's own wiring of that checker into the required CI gate is a flagged carve-out the next `bootstrap upgrade` will drop."
portable_lesson:
"Ship the coverage table — make every instruction declare its own delivery mechanism and its own checker, with the gaps written in as first-class rows. Two artifacts here already do this and they are the highest-value things in the estate:

1. `docs/traps.md`'s closing table: `| trap | delivered by | deterministic checker |`, where five of seven rows read 'not yet' AND state WHY the checker cannot exist ('a checker would have to know a review was requested, which is PR state, not tree state'). One row reads 'none' in the delivered-by column. A rule whose unenforcement is published stops masquerading as enforcement, and the reason-for-no-checker doubles as the spec for the checker someone eventually writes.

2. `tools/check_doc_routes.py`'s coverage assertion: a route must have at least one of its `when` patterns actually occur in one of its docs, so a doc that stops covering its trigger fails the gate instead of confidently sending a session to a page that no longer answers it. Its author names the failure mode exactly — a decayed route is worse than no route, because the session stops looking. Every kit that routes docs needs this, and its companion restraint is just as portable: `NOTE unrouted:` lines are informational and never fatal, because 'a judgement wired to a hard gate produces an agent inventing routes to make a number go green.'

Both are cheap, generic, and would let any adopter answer this census about itself in one command instead of a subagent read of 376 files."

portable_lesson:
Two, both cheap and both proven here.

(1) THE PR-DIFF-AWARE BORN-RED CARD GATE — the estate's best-performing mechanism, and websites is where it was hardened. The card is the FIRST commit with `Status: in-progress`, which holds the PR red; the strict checker greps for literal needles declared as data in substrate.config.json → session_markers rather than hard-coded in prose; and after a real leak (PR #19 auto-merged on an in-progress card) the CI step was made diff-aware with fetch-depth: 0 ([D-0017]) so it derives THIS PR's card from the diff and a stale `complete` card elsewhere in the tree cannot mask it. Result: 302 of 302 cards carry all four markers, zero stranded in-progress. Every repo in the estate should carry the diff-aware variant, not just the checker.

(2) THE TEMPLATE-INSIDE-THE-README RULE, with its reason attached. websites' .sessions/README.md holds the card template inline and states explicitly: do NOT add a standalone TEMPLATE.md, because the session gate treats every .sessions/*.md except README.md as a card, so the template would itself be scanned as a permanently born-red card. That is a scanner-shaped constraint that will bite every adopter identically, and the fix is one paragraph the kit could ship in its own .sessions/README.md so nobody rediscovers it by turning their gate red.

(3) A one-line currency cross-check, already designed here and not yet built: the kit's release checklist ends with "update the adopter's `kit:` line" but nothing compares that self-report against the vendored bootstrap.py header. Both values are already computed during `check`. websites is currently four versions out of date in docs/current-state.md because of exactly this. Ship the comparison; silent drift becomes an automatic DRIFT row.

The kit's engagement gate scans exactly `EXTRA_SCAN_RELPATHS = ("project.index.json", ".claude/CLAUDE.md")` for unrendered banners and slots - and `_unrendered_findings` does `if not path.is_file(): continue`. So the banner would have held the required check RED if the file had been installed; not installing it is precisely what keeps the gate green. The result: 260 session cards of visibly rigorous discipline (born-red cards, byte-identical verifiers, four-gate evidence, full-64 digest matches) running with zero routed instruction - every rule in this repo is delivered either by CI-after-the-fact or by a document the session must already know to open. The single lane that works is the born-red card gate, which is why the card ritual is the one thing 260 sessions never dropped.
portable_lesson: Make absence a finding, not a skip. The kit already knows `.claude/CLAUDE.md` is load-bearing - it names the exact path in `EXTRA_SCAN_RELPATHS` and scans it for unrendered slots - but the scan `continue`s when the file is missing, so the only failure that fully disables the working agreement is the one failure it cannot see. In an adopted install (`_adoption_evidence` true) a missing `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, a missing `.claude/settings.json` whose hooks block matches the staged template, and a staged-but-never-installed `.substrate/skills/` tree should each be strict findings alongside `enforcement-unwired` and `session-loop-idle` - the gate already has that exact born-red shape and just does not use it here. More generally: any check that validates a file's CONTENT must also assert the file EXISTS wherever the runtime actually reads it, because staging a payload and installing it are different acts and only the second one binds anyone. sim-lab is the proof - it passed every gate for 260 sessions with its working agreement sitting one directory away from where any agent would look.

portable_lesson: Two, both already proven here and neither shipped as a mechanism. (1) **Literal-marker gating works, and the number proves it**: because the gate fails on four exact backticked byte-forms, 503 of 503 session cards carry all four — near-perfect compliance on the one rule that has a checker, in a repo where the advisory-tier rule right next to it left 23 stale claim files behind. portable_lesson: Two things this repo built that the kit should ship to everyone. (1) THE LANDING PATH IS THE GATE: the born-red session card is not a request, it is a physical hold — the kit-owned auto-merge enabler arms card-blind at PR open and a host-owned reconciler (`automerge-card-guard.yml`) DISARMS any PR whose diff carries an `in-progress`/`drafted` card, so "first commit is the card, last commit flips it complete" cannot be skipped and the red is designed rather than a failure. That converts the single most-ignored piece of session hygiene from prose into a property of the merge button. Its hardening is portable too: #176 made the disarm provenance-stamped so it survives the auto-merge TOCTOU race. (2) RELOCATE HOST CI OUT OF KIT-OWNED FILES: this repo's only test CI once lived as a hand edit INSIDE the kit-owned gate workflow, one regen away from silent deletion; moving it to its own `tests.yml` made every subsequent upgrade report "carve-out scan: 0 found". The generalisable rule is that an adopter should never edit a kit-owned file — it should add a sibling file the kit does not own — and the carve-out scanner exists to make that violation visible before the regen, not after. A third, smaller one worth shipping: the kit should expose machine-readable tokens (e.g. `HOLD:in-progress`) instead of prose banners, because adopter tests that assert on kit stdout wording red every upgrade PR for second-order reasons — exactly what cost this repo the #183/#184 round trip.

biggest_gap: The boot file is at an address nothing dials. `.substrate/claude/CLAUDE.md` is the kit's staged copy; Claude Code loads `<root>/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, and this repo has no `.claude/` directory at all — no settings.json, no hooks, no doc-routes, no skills. So the working agreement, the boot read order, the preflight-to-HEAD step, the CAPABILITIES discovery rule and the RESEARCH-ONLY rail are all written down and delivered to nobody. This is exactly the failure mode fleet-manager's own boot file describes as "case two" (root is a satellite repo, hub apparatus goes quiet with no error) — except worse, because here there is no satellite apparatus either: the quiet is total and equally silent. The compounding part is that what survives IS the load-bearing stuff. The two rules whose violation would destroy the repo's meaning — never touch real money, and pre-register before you run — are the two with the weakest mechanisms (prose in an unloaded file; "enforced by convention" in the repo's own words). What is well enforced is the paperwork: born-red cards, doc hygiene, pytest. The repo built a real gate around session bookkeeping and left its scientific integrity to good intentions. It got away with it because 5,940 configurations promoted 0 — a null result is not a tempting one to fake. A program that had produced a near-miss would have been testing that convention for real.
portable_lesson: Make the wrong thing unreachable instead of forbidden. This repo's holdout discipline is not a rule — `trading_lab.data.load_ohlcv` will not return bars past HOLDOUT_START, and the paper lane gets a physically separate loader with no unlock parameter. A session cannot peek at the holdout by being careless, or by being clever, or by not having read the file that says not to. Set that beside the same repo's pre-registration rule, which is stated just as forcefully and is, in the repo's own admission, "enforced by convention" — and which nothing in eleven rounds ever checked. Same author, same document, same conviction; one of them survives a session that never read it and the other does not. The kit should ship this as the test applied to every rule it carries: name the function that makes the violation return an error. If no such function can exist, the rule needs a hook that fires at the moment of the action, and if that is impossible too, the rule should be recorded honestly as a hope rather than shipped as a constraint. A corollary this repo demonstrates painfully: check that the instruction file is at a path the harness actually loads before counting anything in it as delivered. A one-line adopter check — does `.claude/CLAUDE.md` exist and is it current with `.substrate/claude/CLAUDE.md`? — would have caught, at adoption time, that this repo's entire working agreement had never once been read by the sessions it governed.

biggest_gap: CLAUDE.md's central design claim — "Everything else is routed, not front-loaded" — is unbacked in this repo. Front-loading was deliberately removed (and check_orientation_budget enforces that removal), but the routing that was supposed to replace it does not exist here: shiftlife's .claude/ contains exactly two files, CLAUDE.md and settings.json, with no hooks directory, no doc-routes map, and no skills. The four wired hooks are the kit's own, and the kit's census states plainly that zero of them can block — three fail-open advisories plus one orientation printer. So the three highest-stakes reads in the boot file (CAPABILITIES before declaring a wall, ROUTINES before touching a trigger, SKILLS before improvising a procedure) are delivered by nothing at the moment of action, and the docs they point at are not even present in this snapshot. The estate's own evidence is that this is the failing class: fleet-manager built route_docs.py precisely because a session probed an API and wrote a wall while the working recipe sat in an unrouted doc, and it made the trigger rule its only DENYING hook. shiftlife carries the same rules with none of that apparatus. Secondary gap: everything the repo actually enforces is process hygiene (heartbeat present, card born-red and flipped, docs badged and reachable, no written walls) — nothing enforces product law. The one recorded rule violation in the repo (verlof-advies shipping free against the Pro column, PR #19 stating no charter test) is in the unenforced half, and the enforced half was green throughout.
portable_lesson: Ship the checker's own honesty about its teeth, and make it readable at the point of use. The kit's HOOK_CENSUS labels every hook ADVISORY / ENFORCING / ORIENTATION with a >15-char reason, keeps EXPECTED_HOOK_ADVISORY = 3 as an anti-shrinkage anchor, and provides hook_enforcing_keys() that is deliberately empty today — so "is anything actually stopping me?" is answerable from data rather than from prose, and gutting the guard set trips a red. STRICT_SUBCHECKS does the same for the checker surface, with a parity test asserting set-equality against the live call sites so a check cannot be dropped or renamed silently. Pair that with shiftlife's control/ pattern of naming src/engine/grammar.py as the single source of truth that the writing doc, the checker, and the /intake skill all consume (pinned by tests/test_grammar.py), and you get the general rule the estate should ship everywhere: every stated rule declares its delivery mechanism and its enforcement class inline, that declaration is generated from the code rather than written beside it, and a shrinkage anchor makes silently removing enforcement louder than leaving it in place. The complement shiftlife proves by absence: a repo's boot file must not use the word "routed" unless a routing map exists in that repo's own .claude/ — a hub-only hook does not bind a satellite session, and prose that claims routing is worse than prose that admits it is prose.

21 numbered invariants, framed as 'violating any of these is a defect, not a style choice'. Discord/permissions: never request Administrator; the bot never DMs members first; the tester role is NEVER granted by code (it mirrors the real Google Play opt-in cohort — only a human can confirm it, and code that grants it inflates the one number the project is ranked against).

AI safety architecture: spiderbot/ai/gateway.py is the single fault boundary and never raises (every failure degrades to a reasoned AIResult); all user-originated text is wrapped via spiderbot/ai/safety.py with kinded <<<UNTRUSTED_DATA__...__BEGIN/END>>> markers, forgery-disarmed, before reaching the model; the AI never performs side effects (role grants, announcements, moderation only via deterministic permission-gated slash commands); unconfigured = silent (initiative replies only in channels named in AI_INITIATIVE_CHANNELS); deterministic without AI (with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY absent or AI_ENABLED=false every command and listener still works).

Mention/ping discipline: every send uses AllowedMentions.none() except the welcome-ping and /announce ping_testers; those two spell out everyone=False, roles=..., users=..., replied_user=False explicitly at the call site rather than inheriting narrowness from the client-wide default, because unset AllowedMentions fields are a sentinel that reads as True; mention detection uses message.mentions and never mentioned_in() (true for @everyone — the estate's BUG-0019 false-ping class).

Layering and UI: ui/ never imports cogs/ (cogs -> ui -> presets/roster/cohort/config); no dead surfaces (every route in ui/routes.py has a _do_<key> handler on HomePanel, and no button is shown to a viewer below its audience floor); rendering is not authorisation (every panel callback re-resolves the presser's standing from live Discord state); Back rebuilds from live state rather than replaying a snapshot (a snapshot would be invariant 15 through the back door); nothing reaches the server unpreviewed (preset posting shows exact text + destination, then requires a confirm press).

Style is code, not taste: colour and emoji come only from spiderbot/style.py — no stock discord.Color.*, nothing outside the eleven-emoji locked vocabulary on a public surface, orange means 'needs your attention' and nothing else, and the AI never speaks without the purple accent + speech balloon.

Observability: every AI decision leaves exactly one audit event (stdout JSON; replies, degrades and tester actions also to #mod-log as embeds); ordinary logs to stdout, problems to stderr via configure_logging — basicConfig would put routine boot chatter and a real crash in the same red bucket on the host, which is the same as having no error signal.
Secrets are env references only — never in code, config files, logs or exception text; .env.example carries names with empty values.
Cog portability (OD-19): plain commands.Cog classes with async def setup(bot), so existing superbot cogs port with only slight alteration.
Verify command: ruff check . + python -m pytest + python -m compileall spiderbot must all pass.

Deploy discipline: push to main IS the deploy (Railway auto-deploys the spider-bot worker) — verify the new deployment's meta.commitHash equals HEAD; railway.json watch patterns mean docs- or tests-only commits deliberately do not deploy and a lagging commitHash is correct, not a failure (absent watch patterns once restarted a donor's production worker ~293 times in one billing cycle); never leave a local instance running while the Railway worker is up (two live bots answering in the real server).

The adopt step planted the *documentation* of the substrate discipline (~400 lines of protocol across control/, .sessions/, .substrate/claude/) and none of the *apparatus*: no .claude/, no hooks, no settings.json, no skills, no doc-routes, no bootstrap.py, no CI workflow, and no root CLAUDE.md — so the working agreement is not even on the auto-load path (it sits at .substrate/claude/CLAUDE.md). Every mechanism the prose names as its enforcer — `check --strict`, the Stop-hook heartbeat reminder, `check_claims`, substrate-gate.yml, the shared src/engine/grammar.py constants — is a reference to a file that is not in this repo. This is PL-013 in its purest form: readable is not binding, and here nothing is even readable without being sought. It is also self-admitted rather than hidden: control/status.md says `phase: adopted — first session not yet run`, `check: red`, `engaged: no`, and both prose docs still carry the ⚠️ UNRENDERED banner with live ${...} slots (${verify_command} among them — the repo literally cannot state how to verify a change). The consequence for the estate census: creator-kit contributes rules to the fleet's stated surface and enforcement to none of it, and a session that boots with creator-kit as its working root (case two of the hub boot triad) gets neither the hub's apparatus nor this repo's, with no error.
portable_lesson: Adoption should plant apparatus first and prose second, and should refuse to look adopted until it has. creator-kit demonstrates the failure mode cleanly: `bootstrap adopt` seeded ~400 lines of binding-status protocol whose every named enforcer is absent, producing a repo that reads fully governed and is governed by nothing. Two shippable fixes fall out. (1) The kit should plant a minimal always-on boot surface at adopt time — a root CLAUDE.md (or .claude/ with settings.json) that at minimum auto-loads and states 'this adoption is unrendered/unengaged; the checkers named below do not run here yet' — because a working agreement stashed at .substrate/claude/CLAUDE.md is a document nothing delivers, which is the exact defect the estate's own intent.md § 4 names ('the fix for an unfollowed rule is a mechanism that delivers it at the right moment, never another statement of it'). (2) Every doc the kit plants that cites an enforcer should be planted *by* that enforcer's installer, not independently — if control/README.md ships without bootstrap.py, the sentence 'the kit enforces this loop' is false on arrival, and a stale-truth claim planted at adopt time is worse than no doc, because it stops the next session from asking whether the loop is enforced. A generalizable check: for each mechanism named in planted prose, assert the file exists in the adopter tree, and fail adopt loudly (or downgrade the doc's Status badge from `binding` to `aspirational`) when it does not.
